title: Palpitations
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is an older woman with hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide who presents with palpitations, syncope, dizziness, and hypotension. ECG demonstrates complete heart block (3rd degree AV block) — complete dissociation between P waves and QRS complexes with no relationship. This is a bradycardic rhythm. Third-degree AV block has an extensive differential: coronary ischemia (most common), fibrosis/sclerosis of conduction system (Lenegre/Lev disease — likely in this patient given age and HTN), Lyme disease, sarcoidosis, hyperkalemia, thyroid disorders, iatrogenic (AV nodal blockers), and congenital (unlikely — 90% symptomatic by age 30). TSH normal, troponin negative, chemistries normal, ESR normal, CBC normal — infectious and inflammatory causes unlikely. Most likely: fibrous degeneration of conduction system from aging + hypertension. Management: temporary transcutaneous/transvenous pacemaker, then permanent pacemaker placement.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Bradycardic rhythm. Regular but slow. No relationship between atrial and ventricular contractions. Cannon A waves may be present in JVP.

decoys.label: Atropine as sole therapy
decoys.reason_wrong: Atropine is ineffective in 3rd degree heart block (infranodal). Definitive treatment is pacing.

decoys.label: Discharge on oral medications
decoys.reason_wrong: Symptomatic complete heart block requires permanent pacemaker. Cannot be managed medically.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Complete AV dissociation — P waves and QRS complexes have no relationship. Atrial rate > ventricular rate. Bradycardic escape rhythm.
Check troponin (ischemia), TSH (thyroid), lyme titer, chemistries (K), ESR (inflammation). Most common cause is coronary ischemia involving conduction system.
Stabilize with transcutaneous or transvenous temporary pacing. Definitive: permanent pacemaker. NPO, pre-op labs.

teach_me_steps.order: Admit to ICU/inpatient with cardiac monitoring
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Complete heart block requires monitored bed. ICU appropriate for temporary pacing management.

case_summary: Complete (3rd degree) AV block — likely fibrotic degeneration from aging + HTN. ECG: P and QRS dissociation. Troponin negative, TSH normal, chemistries normal, ESR normal — infectious/inflammatory unlikely. Temporary pacer → permanent pacemaker. ER → ICU/inpatient.
